explanation: Germany and Austria-Hungary brought it in nationwide in 1916 to save coal during the First World War. Farmers often opposed it, because cows and crops ignore the clock.

claims.text: Daylight saving time was not introduced for the benefit of farmers.
Germany and Austria-Hungary introduced daylight saving time nationwide in 1916 to save fuel, including coal, during the First World War.
Many farmers opposed daylight saving time because their animals and crops keep to the Sun, not the clock.
